statement_summary: Security Lead and TSA Security Coordinators; TSA told of changes within 37 days; one coordinator reachable 24/7
Annual risk assessment with SP 800-30, and after major changes
Risk acceptance authority; High and safety risks never accepted
Sanctions recorded; good-faith reporting protected
Vendor terms reviewed before data or access; 24-hour incident notice in new contracts; annual review of key vendors
Annual independent assessment
Retention of security records; hazmat security plan kept current
Annual policy review; policies available to staff
Written, risk-rated, time-limited exceptions
Check TSA, hazmat security, and PTC duties before new customers, commodities, or movements
Unique accounts; shared crew login replaced by 2026-11-30
Least privilege; dispatcher role only for qualified dispatchers; separate admin accounts
MFA everywhere including MSP-held logins and the telematics portal; number matching
Termination checklist completed by the last day; shared secrets changed
Monthly account reconciliation; quarterly role check
10-minute lock; dispatch desktop unlocked only while staffed
Sealed emergency administrator credential
Named MSP and vendor accounts with MFA; technician list; dispatcher approval for remote work on the dispatch desktop
Password length; yearly Wi-Fi password change; no default passwords
Company systems for company work
No Restricted information in personal accounts or public AI tools
Lock screens; never share passwords or MFA codes; never approve an unexpected MFA prompt
Training at hire and yearly; phishing simulations
Report suspected incidents at once
Confirm payment and bank detail changes by phone
Signed policy acknowledgment
Ransomware runbook kept and printed in the incident binder
Report suspected incidents within 1 hour; tell the dispatcher about anything affecting dispatch
Safety first: switch to paper dispatch with a radio roll call when the system is in doubt
Report cyber attacks to TSA within 24 hours of discovery (company target 12 hours)
Inform TSA promptly of any SSI release
Meet the deadlines in the P08 notification matrix
Insurer hotline first; MSP engaged under contract
Ransom payment only with approvals and an OFAC check
Log every incident with the discovery time
Vendor incident reports logged and handled
Annual tabletop with the MSP; paper dispatch drill twice a year
Lessons learned within 30 days
Three classification levels
SSI access, storage, marking, disposal, and release reporting
Encrypt Restricted information at rest and in transit
Restricted information only in approved locations; security plan by need to know
Inventory of devices, radio and telematics components, SaaS accounts, and data locations
New tools approved before receiving company information
Approved AI tools only
90-day immutable backups; weekly operations data export; quarterly restore test
Wipe or certified destruction with records
Retention of operations and security records
